# Incident Report — 2022-01-07 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
- **IPv4:** 192.168.1.216
- **MAC:** 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9
- **Windows hostname:** DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (confirmed via DHCP hostname option and Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString; NBNS shows a visually similar variant `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2`, an OCR/rendering artifact of the same name)
- **Logged-in domain user:** `steve.smith` (Kerberos CNameString, domain `spoonwatch.net`, DC `SPOONWATCH-DC` at 192.168.1.2)

## Malware Family
**Vidar Stealer** — **behavioral attribution** (no string literally named "Vidar" was observed; identification rests on TTPs and log-format fingerprint that are distinctive of Vidar, not proof by static signature).

Evidence for attribution:
- The single C2 session (tcp.stream 65, port 80) downloaded a batch of legitimate Mozilla NSS/SQLite support libraries — `nss3.dll`, `freebl3.dll`, `mozglue.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, and a `sqlite3`-linked module — disguised with `.jpg` extensions. Bundling these specific DLLs is a well-documented Vidar technique used to decrypt Firefox/NSS-based credential stores on the victim.
- The stealer subsequently exfiltrated a ZIP archive (via `POST /osk/`) with the exact folder/file layout characteristic of Vidar logs: `autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/`, `passwords.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `system.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`.
- All 7 payload downloads and the log exfiltration occurred over one bare-IP HTTP endpoint with no legitimate domain resolution, consistent with Vidar's typical C2 pattern of direct-to-IP panels.

Note: `am_delta_patch_...exe` and the `.cab` files fetched from `au.download.windowsupdate.com` / `download.windowsupdate.com` (Akamai IPs 23.38.189.201/225, 8.253.189.126) are legitimate Windows Defender signature updates — benign, not part of the infection chain.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (TCP stream 65, HTTP, no TLS, no domain — direct IP)

**Malicious URLs (all on the single C2 session)**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (GET, initial panel check-in — evidence: HTTP request log, frame time 207.67s)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` (POST — evidence: HTTP request log, frame time 206.60s)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` (POST requests that retrieve PE payloads mislabeled as `image/jpeg` — evidence: `Content-Type: image/jpeg` responses whose bodies begin with `MZ...This program cannot be run in DOS mode`, confirmed via `file` on exported objects)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (POST, multipart file upload of stolen data — evidence: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="_5861695120.zip"`, `Content-Type: zip`, body signature `PK\x03\x04`)

**Malicious domains:** none observed. The C2 channel used a bare IP with no supporting DNS lookup in the capture.

**Transferred files (downloaded to victim, disguised as `.jpg`) with SHA256:**
| File | SHA256 | Type |
|---|---|---|
| 1.jpg | 16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660 | PE32 DLL (console) |
| 2.jpg | a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba | PE32 DLL (`nss3.dll`/`freebl3.dll`, GUI) |
| 3.jpg | 3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd | PE32 DLL (`mozglue.dll`, GUI) |
| 4.jpg | 334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4 | PE32 DLL (console) |
| 5.jpg | e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78 | PE32 DLL (SQLite-linked, GUI) |
| 6.jpg | 43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083 | PE32 DLL (`softokn3.dll`/`nss3.dll`, GUI) |
| 7.jpg | c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d | PE32 DLL (console) |

**Exfiltrated file (uploaded from victim to C2):**
- `_5861695120.zip` — stolen-data archive containing `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt`. SHA256 of the raw uploaded HTTP object: `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f`.

## Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user `steve.smith` on the `spoonwatch.net` AD domain, was infected with Vidar Stealer. Over a single HTTP session to `2.56.57.108:80`, the malware downloaded seven auxiliary DLLs (disguised as `.jpg` files) needed to decrypt browser-stored credentials, then exfiltrated a ZIP archive of stolen autofill data, cookies, saved passwords, an Outlook account file, a screenshot, and system information to the same C2 IP via `POST /osk/`.
